_comment: THE TOE (docs/plan_early_game_labor.md 'Equipment / TOE', docs/plan_hunt_through_combat.md 4.8). TWO NOUNS, AND THEY ARE NOT THE SAME: an ITEM is a piece of equipment (spears, sled, baskets, traps) that owns its own effects, its own durability and its own use quantum; a KIT is a roster entry that LISTS the items a party is sent out with. The items used to be named `hunting_kit`/`sled_kit`/`basket_kit`, which called both concepts 'kit' and made a kit look like a leaf; they are `items` now and 'kit' means only the roster entry. Consumable, START-STOCKED and NOT CRAFTABLE: running one dry is the intended pressure and the pull into the Milestone-2 crafting economy. TWO TIERS, NEVER A TAPER: performance is FLAT until expiry and then the role STEPS DOWN - durability and performance are deliberately ORTHOGONAL axes so a future crafting system can tune them independently. THE TIER IS PER-BAND, PER-ROLE, not per-hunter inventory. WEAR IS CHARGED FOR USE, NEVER FOR TURNS ELAPSED (docs/plan_denial_raid.md 1.2): a turn clock would charge an idle march the same as a slaughter, which would make denial free. QUALITY TIERS (flint vs bronze spears) are NOT here: they are unobtainable until something can craft them, so they ride the crafting slice. PLAYTEST DIALS.
_comment_effects: AN EFFECT NAMES THE VALUE A STAT TAKES, never a delta and never a multiplier stacking on something else - that is what keeps 'flat until expiry, then a step down' structurally true instead of a rule someone has to remember. Each effect declares exactly ONE tier, and WHICH tier it declares is the one-home-per-fact rule showing through: the OTHER tier already had a home and keeps it. `equipped` = the value while the item is intact, so the baseline lives elsewhere (attack's bare-handed 1.0 is creatures.json `person.combat.attack`; dispersion and exposure are both NEUTRAL AT 1.0, which is why an item that does not mention them changes nothing). `unequipped` = the value once the item is spent, so the equipped value lives elsewhere (the hunt's 40.0 is labor_config.json `hunt.per_worker_biomass_capacity`, the gather's 8.0 its `forage.per_worker_biomass_capacity` - the rates the shipped, start-kitted game has always run on). Copying either into this file would give a shipped number a second home to drift from.
_comment_shapes: THE TWO CARRY ITEMS WANT DIFFERENT SHAPES, NOT MERELY DIFFERENT NUMBERS (4.8). FORAGE IS CONTAINMENT-BOUND - bare hands is a handful against a basketful - so its ratio is LARGE: 8.0 equipped against 1.6 bare, exactly one fifth, which is about what a forager keeps when the only vessel is two cupped hands and the fold of a hide. THE HUNT IS TRANSPORT-BOUND - a sledless party can always drag SOMETHING - so its ratio is SMALLER: 40.0 equipped against 12.0, under a third. The hunt's shortfall needs no new mechanic: a party that cannot haul its kill leaves more of it on the range, which AnimalTake.wasted already computes and the client already shows.
_comment_declaring_the_neutral: SPEARS DECLARE `dispersion 1.0` AND `exposure 1.0` THOUGH BOTH ARE THE NEUTRAL VALUE, and that is load-bearing rather than noise. A kit resolves a multiplier stat as the MAXIMUM of what its LIVE items DECLARE, and an item that says nothing contributes nothing (not the neutral) - which is what stops the sled, carry gear nobody approaches an animal with, from dragging a trapping party's dispersion back to 1.0 just by being in the kit. The declaration is therefore what makes a spears-AND-traps kit resolve to LOUD and EXPOSED instead of inheriting the trap's stand-off for free: if you are running up throwing spears you are scaring the herd and you are in reach of it, however many traps you also set. Nothing shipped pairs them today; the declaration is what keeps the answer right the day something does.
_comment_traps: THE PASSIVE DEVICE - snares, nets, weirs, all one item because at this game's abstraction they are one thing: something you set down, walk away from, and come back to. Whether a given device holds one animal or a whole run, and whether it is discriminate, is detail the game never surfaces; two items separated by numbers that mean nothing would be worse than one honest one. ITS WHOLE ADVANTAGE IS `dispersion 0` - it is not there to be seen, so nothing bolts and the party keeps everything it reaches. Against a Rabbit Warren at `wariness 0.75` a spear party loses three animals in four to the retreat and this loses none, which is the entire 50 -> 200 gap. ITS `attack` IS THE SPEAR'S OWN NUMBER, and that is the point rather than a coincidence: at 0.13-0.67 kg the weapon is not what is scarce, so the device must not win by hitting harder - it wins by not scaring anything. `max_body_mass` is what keeps it off everything else. NO REACH MULTIPLIER: a x4 was authored here and MEASURED INERT - the fight binds before reach does on every small-game row (reach/worker `engage_rate x mult` against fight/worker `attack / durability` is 40 vs 10 on a rabbit, 60 vs 10 on a catfish), so it changed no outcome anywhere. The stat was REMOVED rather than shipped neutral: a lever with no effect is worse than no lever, and the thing it superficially resembled - an archer reaching what it cannot close with - is `RangeBand` on the combat resolver, reserved for the ranged pre-phase on #501. Re-add it the day something genuinely raises reach (dogs, a drive), with its own justification and its own test.
_comment_dispersion: DISPERSION MULTIPLIES THE QUARRY'S OWN FLIGHT RESPONSE: effective_wariness = clamp(wariness * dispersion, 0, 1), and stayers = engaged * (1 - effective_wariness). It is NEUTRAL AT 1.0, so every item that does not declare it - and every kit that carries no item declaring it - leaves the shipped retreat untouched. TRAPS SHIP 0.0: a trap line does not scare anything, because nothing runs up to the animal. THE SPECIES DECIDES HOW MUCH IT MATTERS, which is the whole reason this is a multiplier and not a subtraction: a Gazelle at wariness 0.85 loses almost everything to a noisy approach while a Mammoth at 0.10 barely notices, so ONE spear line scatters a warren and contains a mammoth with no special-casing and no per-target authoring. wariness 0 is already an exact identity in the retreat (no draw is made), so dispersion 0 lands in a regime the sim has always had rather than a new one.
_comment_mass_bound: A SNARE HOLDS A HARE AND NOT A DEER, which `dispersion` cannot say: dispersion answers *does the animal bolt before you reach it*, a different question from *what can this thing physically hold*. Collapsing the two is what made a flat `attack 8` take Red Deer - a deer's `defense` is 1, so a trap cleared it like everything else's. `max_body_mass` bounds the effect to quarry it can actually hold; above it the item contributes NO attack, the party falls back to the bare hand's 1, and `max(0, 1 - defense)` is the EXISTING gate refusing the hunt. No new rule, no 'cannot trap that' branch. IT READS `body_mass`, WHICH THE ROSTER ALREADY AUTHORS, NOT A SIZE CATEGORY - a `size_class` here would be a second authority to drift from the masses, exactly as `dispersion` reads `wariness` rather than a 'jumpy' flag. The shipped roster separates cleanly: every `defense 0` row is 0.13-0.67 (fowl, rabbit, grouse, snow hare, catfish) and the next species up is a Desert Gazelle at 3.3, so ANY ceiling in that gap behaves identically and 1.0 is the round number in it. `min_body_mass` is the same field's other end - a bow is poor against something small and fast - and is reserved for the ranged work on #501; nothing ships one. ONLY `attack` IS RESOLVED AGAINST A QUARRY TODAY, so a bound on any other stat is REJECTED at validate rather than silently ignored.
_comment_exposure: EXPOSURE IS WHETHER THE ITEM'S USERS ARE IN REACH OF THE ANIMAL, and it multiplies the hunt's baseline injury hazard (fauna::hunt_injuries = combat_config.hunt_injury_damage_per_animal * animals engaged * lethality). NEUTRAL AT 1.0. TRAPS SHIP 0.0 - a trap is a stand-off instrument, so it wears out INSTEAD of the trapper getting hurt, which is the trade and not a free lunch. It is deliberately NOT a weapon-vs-gear classification: what matters is whether the users are exposed, because that is what the resolver keys casualties on.
_comment_durability: DURABILITY IS A 0-100 CONDITION SCALE ON EVERY ITEM, and the per-use wear rate is what says how long each lasts - that is what keeps the two axes orthogonal (change how long an item lasts without touching what it does). A band carries WEAR (BandEquipment, persisted); an item is EQUIPPED while its wear is strictly below its starting_durability, and the drop at expiry is a cliff. Spears: 100 / 0.4 per kill = 250 kills. Sled: 100 / 0.02 per biomass hauled = 5000 biomass. Baskets: 100 / 0.04 per biomass gathered = 2500 biomass. Traps: 100 / 0.2 per kill = 500 kills, twice the spear's life per kill because a trap is worked rather than thrown - and it is charged on the SAME quantum as spears so a trapping party cannot hunt for free. AGAINST THE SHIPPED ~16-WORKER STARTING BAND THE BASKET HITS plan_early_game_labor's ~15-20 TURN KIT-DURATION TARGET AND THE TWO HUNT ITEMS OVERSHOOT IT BY ~3x (gathering reaches 16 x 8 = 128 biomass a turn, so 2500/128 = ~19.5 turns of baskets; hunting Red Deer the retreat leaves ~5.6 kills a turn, so 250/5.6 = ~45 turns of spears and 5000/(5.6 x 15) = ~60 turns of sled). Closing that gap is a balance change, not a comment fix, and it belongs with the hunt-effectiveness tuning tracked on issue #495. THE QUANTA ARE INDEPENDENT BY CONSTRUCTION: a band that only hunts wears no baskets and a band that only gathers wears no sled. KNOWN SKEW, a config problem not a model one: a per-KILL charge is species-blind, so a party on Wild Fowl shreds the same spears in ~4.5 turns. The quantum is deliberate (docs/plan_denial_raid.md 1.2 requires wear to track USE, and for a spear a use IS a kill); if small game proves to wreck the pacing, the lever is a per-species use cost, not a turn clock.
_comment_husbandry: HUSBANDRY GEAR - hurdles, halters, a butchering stone, vessels. WHAT BOUNDS A PEN IS HANDLING, NOT DRAGGING, which is why it declares `pen_carry` and not the sled's `hunt_carry`: a sled brings a carcass in off the range, and a pen is at the camp. A pen harvest has always been capped by the same 40.0 the wild hunt is (labor_config.json `hunt.per_worker_biomass_capacity`), so that number stays where it is and this item declares only the OTHER side - 12.0, a keeper working a pen with whatever is to hand. THE CONSEQUENCE IS DELIBERATE AND IS THE POINT OF THE KIT: a band that corrals a herd and leaves the assignment on `big_game` is working its pen with a drag harness and no handling gear, and collects at 12 rather than 40. That is the same mistake as bringing baskets to a deer, and the roster exists so the player can stop making it. ITS QUANTUM IS `biomass_collected`, NOT `biomass_hauled`, though a pen charges both: the sled is being dragged and this is being worked, so a band that only keeps pens must never blunt a sled it did not take onto the range. 100 / 0.08 = 1250 biomass, roughly the basket's clock against a pen's steadier, smaller take.
_comment_wayfinding: WAYFINDING GEAR - tallies, marked staves, a fire-drill, whatever a forward observer carries. IT LIFTS WHAT A VANTAGE CAN MAKE OUT (`scout_vantage_range`), NOT HOW FAR OUT IT IS POSTED: the posting distance is three dials (labor_config.json `scout.vantage_distance_base` / `_per_scout` / `_max`) and a kit reaching into one of them would be a fourth authority over the same line. The equipped 2 is labor_config's `scout.vantage_range` and stays there; this declares the bare 1.0. ITS QUANTUM IS `tile_revealed`, AND `tile_revealed` MEANS FIRST-EVER-REVEALED. A parked band re-sees the same ring every turn, so charging per tile SEEN would be a turn clock in a per-use costume - precisely what docs/plan_denial_raid.md 1.2 forbids. What wears wayfinding gear is going somewhere new, so a band that stops exploring stops paying, and a band that never explores pays nothing at all. 100 / 0.05 = 2000 first-sights.
_comment_warrior: CLUBS - the Warrior role's TOE, and the arc's 'weapons -> combat strength / rocks and fists -> weak force' made real. IT DECLARES `attack` - THE SAME STAT A SPEAR DOES - because attack is already 'what this person hits with' and a `warrior_attack` beside it would be a second authority over the one number the resolver reads. What keeps a club out of a hunt and a spear out of a raid is the kit's `jobs` list. Equipped 6.0 against the bare hand's 1.0 (creatures.json `person.combat.attack`), well under the spear's 20: a raid is people fighting animals at the camp with whatever is by the fire, not a hunting party that chose its ground. THIS IS THE ONE PLACE THE SHIPPED OPENING MOVES - a start-kitted band defends a predator raid at 6 where it used to defend at 1, and drops back to 1 when the clubs are gone. Predators Phase 1b is explicitly a placeholder resolver, so the raid tuning is the right place to absorb it. ITS QUANTUM IS `fight` - ONE ENGAGEMENT, ONE USE, not one casualty inflicted: a defence that killed nothing was still fought, and pricing gear on its results would charge a band that is losing the least. 100 / 2.0 = 50 raids fought.
_comment_kits: THE KIT ROSTER - what a party is SENT OUT WITH, chosen by name instead of implicitly using whatever the band owns. A kit is a MASK over the items above: effective_equipped(item) = kit uses it AND the band still has condition in it. `big_game` and `gathering` reproduce the pre-roster behaviour exactly, so choosing them is bit-for-bit the shipped game. `none` is an ORDINARY ROSTER MEMBER and NOT a sentinel: it simply uses nothing, so every predicate reads false and the party runs at the unequipped tiers throughout - and, because wear rides the same predicate, spends no durability on any item. That is what makes a bare-handed comparison free to run: it must not consume the very kit it is being compared against. `trapping` is the first kit that is not a subset of the old behaviour: traps clear no defence (a trapper falls back to the bare hand's attack 1), so it takes ONLY quarry with no defence at all - rabbit, fowl, grouse, snow hare, catfish - and on exactly that quarry it is the better instrument, because reach and not damage is what binds there. It carries the sled too: a trapper still has to get the catch home. `jobs` is what a kit may be sent on; a kit named for a job it does not list is a COMMAND FAILURE, never a silent fall back to the default. `default_kits` is what each verb uses when the player names none. THE BAND-WIDE ROLES NOW HAVE A KIT AXIS: `scout` and `warrior` are jobs like the other two. They were absent on the grounds that they consumed no component, which was a statement about this file and not about the sim - scouts have posted forward-observer vantages and warriors have been the band's defending contingent against a predator raid for some time. `none` lists all four, so going bare is a choice on every role.
